title: Anatomy at Gray's depth: bone, joint, muscle, fat and surface
reads_with: human-canon.json (landmarks and widths in heads), construction.json (how to build the forms), sources/gray1918/excerpts.json (the Gray passages)
how_to_use: Model bone first: put every surface landmark where the canon puts it. Rig the joints with the types and ranges below. Lay the muscles by their origin and insertion (they decide the direction of every bulge), then the fat pads for the sex and build, then check the surface list for each view. Score with the checklist.

sources.gray1918: Henry Gray, Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th edition, revised by Warren H. Lewis (Lea & Febiger, 1918). Public domain. Read from the Wikisource transcription; each muscle and joint links to its scan page.
sources.rom: Ranges of motion: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons averages as given in Norkin and White, Measurement of Joint Motion. Gray (1918) names each movement but gives few degrees.
sources.fat: Fat pad placement from Gray (1918, superficial fascia) and artistic anatomy (Richer, Artistic Anatomy, 1890); thickness from adult skinfold norms (half a skinfold), rounded.
sources.plates: Plates drawn by tools/bodies/anatomy.py from these attachments: anatomical position, the canon man, right half drawn and mirrored.

landmarks.name: frontal eminences
landmarks.form: two soft bosses of the forehead

landmarks.name: superciliary arches
landmarks.form: brow ridge, stronger on a man

landmarks.name: zygomatic arch
landmarks.form: cheekbone ridge running back to the ear

landmarks.name: external occipital protuberance
landmarks.form: bump at the back of the head where the neck meets it

landmarks.name: mastoid process
landmarks.form: knob behind the ear lobe; the sternocleidomastoid starts here

landmarks.name: angle of the mandible
landmarks.form: corner of the jaw, below the ear lobe

landmarks.name: mental protuberance
landmarks.form: the chin

bones.name: Vertebral column (7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, sacrum, coccyx)

landmarks.name: spinous process of C7 (vertebra prominens)
landmarks.form: the first knob felt at the base of the neck

landmarks.name: thoracic spinous processes
landmarks.form: a line of knobs in the back furrow, plainer when bent forward

landmarks.name: lumbar spinous processes
landmarks.form: sunk in a groove between the two erector columns

landmarks.name: sacrum
landmarks.form: flat triangle between the two dimples of Venus

bones.curves: cervical lordosis forward, thoracic kyphosis back, lumbar lordosis forward, sacral curve back

bones.name: Thorax (sternum, 12 pairs of ribs, costal cartilages)

landmarks.name: jugular (suprasternal) notch
landmarks.form: the pit of the neck

landmarks.name: sternal angle
landmarks.form: a cross ridge two fingers below the pit, at the 2nd rib

landmarks.name: xiphoid process
landmarks.form: tip of the breastbone in the pit of the stomach

landmarks.name: costal arch
landmarks.form: the lower rim of the ribcage, an inverted V

landmarks.name: lower ribs on the flank
landmarks.form: serratus and oblique digitations interlock over them

bones.notes: Egg-shaped, narrow above; ribs slope down and forward; the cartilages of ribs 7 to 10 make the costal arch.

landmarks.name: sternal end
landmarks.form: knob on each side of the pit

landmarks.name: shaft
landmarks.form: a shallow S, convex forward on its inner two thirds

landmarks.name: acromial end
landmarks.form: small step at the shoulder point

landmarks.name: acromion
landmarks.form: the shoulder point, the top corner of the shoulder

landmarks.name: spine of the scapula
landmarks.form: a ridge across the upper shoulder blade; shows as a groove in a muscular back

landmarks.name: medial (vertebral) border
landmarks.form: edge of the shoulder blade beside the spine, about 2 inches out

landmarks.name: inferior angle
landmarks.form: the point of the shoulder blade, at the level of the 7th rib

landmarks.name: coracoid process
landmarks.form: felt in the hollow below the outer clavicle

landmarks.name: greater tubercle
landmarks.form: under the deltoid; makes the widest point of the shoulders

landmarks.name: deltoid tuberosity
landmarks.form: halfway down the outer arm, where the deltoid ends

landmarks.name: medial epicondyle
landmarks.form: the sharp inner knob of the elbow

landmarks.name: lateral epicondyle
landmarks.form: the smaller outer knob, in a dimple when the arm is straight

landmarks.name: olecranon
landmarks.form: point of the elbow

landmarks.name: posterior border
landmarks.form: the ulnar furrow along the back of the forearm, bone right under the skin

landmarks.name: head of the ulna
landmarks.form: knob on the little-finger side of the back of the wrist

landmarks.name: styloid process of the ulna
landmarks.form: small point below the head

landmarks.name: head of the radius
landmarks.form: turns under the thumb just below the lateral epicondyle

landmarks.name: styloid process of the radius
landmarks.form: the thumb-side knob of the wrist, lower than the ulnar one

landmarks.name: pisiform
landmarks.form: pea-sized knob at the heel of the hand, little-finger side

landmarks.name: metacarpal heads
landmarks.form: the knuckles, an arc highest at the middle finger

landmarks.name: phalangeal joints
landmarks.form: finger joints, each a little box with a crease over it

bones.name: Hip bone (ilium, ischium, pubis) and sacrum

landmarks.name: iliac crest
landmarks.form: the hip bone ridge; on a lean man the flank pad rolls over it

landmarks.name: anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)
landmarks.form: front point of the hip bone; the inguinal fold starts here

landmarks.name: posterior superior iliac spine
landmarks.form: a dimple of Venus each side of the sacrum

landmarks.name: pubic symphysis
landmarks.form: the midline under the lower belly

landmarks.name: ischial tuberosity
landmarks.form: the sitting bone, under the gluteal fold

bones.notes: Wider, shallower and tilted further forward in a woman: the trochanters become the widest point.

landmarks.name: greater trochanter
landmarks.form: a flat or hollow spot on the side of the hip, a hand below the iliac crest

landmarks.name: shaft
landmarks.form: slants in about 10 degrees from hip to knee (more on a woman)

landmarks.name: femoral condyles
landmarks.form: the sides of the knee; the inner one lower and bigger

landmarks.name: adductor tubercle
landmarks.form: small knob above the inner condyle

landmarks.name: patella
landmarks.form: a rounded triangle, point down; sits above the knee joint line when straight

landmarks.name: tibial tuberosity
landmarks.form: a bump a hand below the kneecap; the patellar ligament ends on it

landmarks.name: anterior border (shin)
landmarks.form: the shin: a sharp edge, slightly S-shaped, bone right under the skin

landmarks.name: medial surface
landmarks.form: flat face of the shin, facing in and forward

landmarks.name: medial malleolus
landmarks.form: the inner ankle bone; higher and further forward than the outer

landmarks.name: head of the fibula
landmarks.form: knob on the outer side just below the knee, where the biceps femoris ends

landmarks.name: lateral malleolus
landmarks.form: the outer ankle bone; lower and further back than the inner

bones.name: Tarsus, metatarsus and phalanges

landmarks.name: calcaneus
landmarks.form: the heel; sticks out behind the leg line

landmarks.name: navicular tuberosity
landmarks.form: knob on the inner arch in front of the ankle

landmarks.name: base of the 5th metatarsal
landmarks.form: knob halfway along the outer edge of the foot

landmarks.name: head of the 1st metatarsal
landmarks.form: the ball of the big toe

bones.notes: Arch on the inner side only; the outer edge rests on the ground.

joints.name: Jaw (temporomandibular)
joints.rig: hinge plus forward slide: the jaw drops and moves forward when the mouth opens wide

joints.name: Neck (atlanto-occipital, atlanto-axial and cervical spine)
joints.rig: nod at the skull, turn at the atlas, the rest spread over C2 to C7

joints.name: Thoracic and lumbar spine
joints.rig: bend mostly in the lumbar spine, turn mostly in the thoracic; the ribcage and pelvis stay rigid

joints.name: Sternoclavicular
joints.rig: the only bony link of the arm to the trunk: the clavicle rises in a shrug and swings in a reach

joints.name: Shoulder blade on the ribcage
joints.gray_type: not a true joint: muscles hold the scapula on the ribs
joints.rig: a third of arm raising is the scapula turning; rotate it, do not only rotate the humerus

joints.name: Shoulder (glenohumeral)
joints.rig: 180 degrees of raising is about 120 here plus 60 from the scapula (2 to 1); the deltoid bunches, the armpit hollow opens

joints.name: Elbow (humero-ulnar and humero-radial)
joints.rig: one hinge axis; forearm angles out in extension (the carrying angle) and lines up with the arm in flexion

joints.name: Forearm (proximal and distal radioulnar)
joints.rig: the radius crosses over the ulna; twist the forearm along its length, never at the wrist

joints.name: Wrist (radiocarpal and midcarpal)
joints.rig: two axes, no twist; bends further to the little-finger side

joints.name: Thumb carpometacarpal
joints.rig: the thumb swings across the palm on its own saddle joint at the wrist

joints.name: Finger joints (interphalangeal)
joints.rig: hinges only; a curling finger makes a spiral toward the base of the thumb

joints.name: Hip
joints.rig: a deep socket: extension is short, so a leg swinging back is helped by the pelvis tilting

joints.name: Knee
joints.gray_type: ginglymus (hinge) with some rotation, a condyloid joint in Gray
joints.rig: locks with a small twist at full extension; the kneecap slides down its groove as it bends

joints.name: Ankle (talocrural)
joints.rig: hinge on a slanted axis through the two malleoli: the foot points slightly out as it flexes

joints.name: Subtalar and midtarsal
joints.rig: the foot rolls in and out here, not at the ankle

joints.name: Toes (metatarsophalangeal)
joints.rig: the toe break: the foot bends here in every step

muscles.name: Masseter
muscles.origin: zygomatic arch
muscles.insertion: angle and outer face of the mandible ramus
muscles.action: closes the jaw
muscles.surface: squares the back of the jaw; bulges when the teeth clench

muscles.name: Temporalis
muscles.origin: temporal fossa
muscles.insertion: coronoid process of the mandible
muscles.action: closes the jaw, pulls it back
muscles.surface: fills the temple; fans out above the ear

muscles.name: Platysma
muscles.origin: fascia over the upper chest
muscles.insertion: lower border of the mandible, skin of the lower face
muscles.action: tenses the neck skin, pulls the mouth corners down
muscles.surface: thin sheet; shows only as vertical cords in strain

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: two heads: front of the manubrium (sternum) and inner third of the clavicle
muscles.insertion: mastoid process and the superior nuchal line
muscles.action: one side: tilts the head to its side and turns the face away; both: flex the neck
muscles.surface: the strap from behind the ear to the pit of the neck; the two make the V of the neck and a hollow between their heads

muscles.name: Scalenes
muscles.origin: transverse processes of C3 to C6
muscles.insertion: first and second ribs
muscles.action: raise the first ribs, bend the neck to the side
muscles.surface: fill the triangle behind the sternocleidomastoid

muscles.name: Splenius capitis
muscles.origin: ligamentum nuchae and spines of C7 to T3
muscles.insertion: mastoid process and the occipital bone
muscles.action: extends the head, turns it to its own side
muscles.nerve: dorsal rami of the middle cervical nerves
muscles.surface: a band under the trapezius at the back of the neck

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.origin: external occipital protuberance, ligamentum nuchae and the spines of C7 to T12
muscles.insertion: outer third of the clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula
muscles.action: upper: shrugs and turns the scapula up; middle: pulls it in; lower: pulls it down
muscles.surface: a kite-shaped sheet; the slope from neck to shoulder; a tendinous diamond at C7 shows as a flat spot

muscles.name: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.origin: spines of T7 to the sacrum by the thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lower ribs and the inferior angle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: floor of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
muscles.action: pulls the arm down, back and inward (climbing, rowing)
muscles.surface: the wing of the back; makes the V taper and the back wall of the armpit

muscles.name: Rhomboids (major and minor)
muscles.origin: spines of C7 to T5
muscles.insertion: medial border of the scapula
muscles.action: pull the scapula toward the spine and up
muscles.surface: under the trapezius; a ridge between the shoulder blades when they pinch together

muscles.name: Levator scapulae
muscles.origin: transverse processes of C1 to C4
muscles.insertion: superior angle of the scapula
muscles.action: lifts the scapula
muscles.nerve: dorsal scapular nerve, C3 and C4
muscles.surface: part of the slope of the neck, behind the sternocleidomastoid

muscles.name: Erector spinae
muscles.origin: sacrum, iliac crest and lumbar spines
muscles.insertion: ribs and spines and transverse processes all the way up to the skull
muscles.action: straightens and arches the back, bends it to the side
muscles.nerve: dorsal rami of the spinal nerves
muscles.surface: two thick columns either side of the spine in the lower back; the furrow lies between them

muscles.name: Pectoralis major
muscles.origin: inner half of the clavicle, front of the sternum, cartilages of ribs 1 to 6 and the external oblique aponeurosis
muscles.insertion: crest of the greater tubercle of the humerus (fibers twist: the lowest insert highest)
muscles.action: pulls the arm across the chest, rotates it in; clavicular part raises it
muscles.nerve: medial and lateral pectoral nerves (Gray: anterior thoracic)
muscles.surface: the chest plate; its lower border is the front wall of the armpit; a clavicular and a sternal part

muscles.name: Pectoralis minor
muscles.origin: ribs 3 to 5
muscles.insertion: coracoid process of the scapula
muscles.action: pulls the scapula forward and down
muscles.surface: hidden; fills out the upper chest under the pectoralis major

muscles.name: Serratus anterior
muscles.origin: outer faces of ribs 1 to 8 or 9
muscles.insertion: medial border of the scapula, front face
muscles.action: pulls the scapula forward round the ribs (punching), turns it up
muscles.surface: saw-tooth fingers on the side of the ribcage below the armpit; 4 show, interlocking with the external oblique

muscles.name: External oblique
muscles.origin: outer faces of the lower 8 ribs, interlocking with the serratus and latissimus
muscles.insertion: front half of the iliac crest and, by its aponeurosis, the linea alba and the inguinal ligament
muscles.action: bends and turns the trunk, compresses the belly
muscles.nerve: lower intercostal nerves (T7 to T12), iliohypogastric
muscles.surface: the flank; its fleshy part ends above the iliac crest in the flank pad; fibers run down and forward like hands in front pockets

muscles.name: Rectus abdominis
muscles.origin: crest of the pubis and the symphysis
muscles.insertion: cartilages of ribs 5 to 7 and the xiphoid
muscles.action: bends the trunk forward
muscles.surface: the "six-pack": three tendinous intersections above the navel (one at it, one at the xiphoid and one between), none below; the lower belly is one smooth form

muscles.name: Deltoid
muscles.origin: outer third of the clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula (the same line the trapezius ends on)
muscles.insertion: deltoid tuberosity, halfway down the outer humerus
muscles.action: raises the arm: front part forward, middle part sideways, back part backward
muscles.surface: caps the shoulder; a thick V wedge into the outer arm; the middle part is multipennate and bulges in bands

muscles.name: Supraspinatus
muscles.origin: supraspinous fossa
muscles.insertion: top facet of the greater tubercle
muscles.action: starts raising the arm
muscles.surface: under the trapezius; fills the hollow above the spine of the scapula

muscles.name: Infraspinatus
muscles.origin: infraspinous fossa
muscles.insertion: middle facet of the greater tubercle
muscles.action: rotates the arm out
muscles.surface: a flat triangle on the shoulder blade below the spine

muscles.name: Teres minor
muscles.origin: upper outer border of the scapula
muscles.insertion: lowest facet of the greater tubercle
muscles.action: rotates the arm out
muscles.surface: a small roll below the infraspinatus

muscles.name: Teres major
muscles.origin: inferior angle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: medial lip of the intertubercular groove
muscles.action: pulls the arm in and back, rotates it in
muscles.surface: a thick roll from the shoulder-blade point into the armpit, above the latissimus

muscles.name: Subscapularis
muscles.origin: subscapular fossa (front face of the scapula)
muscles.insertion: lesser tubercle of the humerus
muscles.action: rotates the arm in
muscles.surface: hidden between the scapula and the ribs

muscles.name: Coracobrachialis
muscles.origin: coracoid process
muscles.insertion: middle of the inner humerus
muscles.action: flexes and adducts the arm
muscles.surface: a small roll in the armpit when the arm is raised

muscles.name: Biceps brachii
muscles.origin: long head: above the glenoid; short head: coracoid process
muscles.insertion: radial tuberosity, and the bicipital aponeurosis into the forearm fascia
muscles.action: bends the elbow and turns the palm up (supinates)
muscles.surface: a long oval on the front of the arm, ending in a cord at the elbow crease; peaks when the palm turns up

muscles.name: Brachialis
muscles.origin: lower half of the front of the humerus
muscles.insertion: coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
muscles.action: bends the elbow
muscles.surface: shows either side of the biceps above the elbow; widens the lower arm from the side

muscles.name: Triceps brachii
muscles.origin: long head: below the glenoid; lateral head: back of the humerus above the radial groove; medial head: below it
muscles.insertion: olecranon of the ulna by a broad flat tendon
muscles.action: straightens the elbow
muscles.surface: a horseshoe on the back of the arm: two heads above a flat tendon plate that fills the lower third

muscles.name: Anconeus
muscles.origin: lateral epicondyle (back)
muscles.insertion: side of the olecranon and the upper ulna
muscles.action: helps straighten the elbow
muscles.surface: a small triangle beside the point of the elbow

muscles.name: Pronator teres
muscles.origin: medial epicondyle and the coronoid process
muscles.insertion: middle of the outer radius
muscles.action: turns the palm down
muscles.surface: the inner edge of the elbow hollow, running across to the outer forearm

muscles.name: Forearm flexors (flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris, flexor digitorum superficialis)
muscles.origin: common flexor origin on the medial epicondyle
muscles.insertion: front of the wrist and hand: 2nd metacarpal, palmar fascia, pisiform, middle phalanges
muscles.action: bend the wrist and fingers
muscles.nerve: median nerve; flexor carpi ulnaris by the ulnar nerve
muscles.surface: the fleshy inner mass of the forearm, bellies in the upper half, tendons below; the palmaris and flexor carpi radialis tendons stand out at the wrist

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus, a third of the way up the arm
muscles.insertion: styloid process of the radius
muscles.action: bends the elbow, most in mid-turn (thumb up)
muscles.surface: the outer bulge just below the elbow; with the extensor carpi radialis it makes the "outer mass" of the forearm, separate from the extensors

muscles.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
muscles.origin: lateral supracondylar ridge and lateral epicondyle
muscles.insertion: bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals
muscles.action: extend the wrist and tilt it to the thumb side
muscles.surface: continue the brachioradialis down the outer forearm

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum and extensor carpi ulnaris
muscles.origin: common extensor origin on the lateral epicondyle
muscles.insertion: extensor expansions of the fingers; base of the 5th metacarpal
muscles.action: straighten the fingers and the wrist
muscles.surface: the back of the forearm; tendons fan over the back of the hand

muscles.name: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
muscles.origin: back of the radius and ulna, middle third
muscles.insertion: base of the thumb metacarpal and its first phalanx
muscles.action: pull the thumb out and back
muscles.surface: a small diagonal ridge crossing the lower radius, toward the thumb

muscles.name: Iliopsoas (psoas major and iliacus)
muscles.origin: lumbar vertebrae and the iliac fossa
muscles.insertion: lesser trochanter
muscles.action: the strongest hip flexor
muscles.surface: deep; shows only in the floor of the triangle below the groin

muscles.name: Sartorius
muscles.origin: anterior superior iliac spine
muscles.insertion: upper inner face of the tibia (pes anserinus)
muscles.action: flexes, abducts and turns out the hip, bends the knee (sitting cross-legged)
muscles.surface: the longest muscle: a strap across the front of the thigh in a long S, dividing the quads from the adductors

muscles.name: Tensor fasciae latae
muscles.origin: outer lip of the iliac crest behind the ASIS
muscles.insertion: iliotibial band
muscles.action: flexes and abducts the hip, steadies the knee
muscles.surface: a short bulge below and behind the hip point

muscles.name: Gluteus medius
muscles.origin: outer ilium below the crest
muscles.insertion: outer greater trochanter
muscles.action: abducts the hip, holds the pelvis level on one leg
muscles.surface: the fullness on the side of the hip above the trochanter, under the iliac crest

muscles.name: Gluteus maximus
muscles.origin: back of the ilium, sacrum, coccyx and the sacrotuberous ligament
muscles.insertion: iliotibial band (most) and the gluteal tuberosity of the femur
muscles.action: extends the hip (climbing, rising, running), turns it out
muscles.surface: the buttock: a thick square slanting down and out; its lower edge is not the gluteal fold (that is fat and skin)

muscles.name: Rectus femoris
muscles.origin: anterior inferior iliac spine and above the acetabulum
muscles.insertion: patella, and on through the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity
muscles.action: extends the knee, flexes the hip
muscles.surface: the middle of the front of the thigh, a long spindle

muscles.name: Vastus lateralis
muscles.origin: greater trochanter and the lateral lip of the linea aspera
muscles.insertion: outer patella and quadriceps tendon
muscles.action: extends the knee
muscles.surface: the big outer thigh; highest bulge on the outside

muscles.name: Vastus medialis
muscles.origin: medial lip of the linea aspera
muscles.insertion: inner patella and quadriceps tendon
muscles.action: extends the knee, steadies the kneecap
muscles.surface: the teardrop above and inside the knee: lower than the outer bulge

muscles.name: Adductors (pectineus, adductor longus, gracilis, adductor magnus)
muscles.origin: pubis and ischium
muscles.insertion: linea aspera of the femur; gracilis to the upper inner tibia
muscles.action: pull the thighs together
muscles.nerve: obturator nerve; the hamstring part of the adductor magnus by the sciatic
muscles.surface: the inner thigh mass, widest near the groin, tapering to the knee

muscles.name: Biceps femoris
muscles.origin: long head: ischial tuberosity; short head: linea aspera
muscles.insertion: head of the fibula
muscles.action: bends the knee, extends the hip, turns the bent knee out
muscles.nerve: sciatic nerve (tibial and common peroneal parts)
muscles.surface: the outer hamstring; its tendon is the cord on the outside of the back of the knee

muscles.name: Semitendinosus and semimembranosus
muscles.origin: ischial tuberosity
muscles.insertion: upper inner tibia (pes anserinus) and the back of the medial tibial condyle
muscles.action: bend the knee, extend the hip, turn the bent knee in
muscles.surface: the inner hamstrings; their tendons are the cords on the inside of the back of the knee

muscles.name: Tibialis anterior
muscles.origin: upper two thirds of the outer tibia
muscles.insertion: medial cuneiform and 1st metatarsal base
muscles.action: lifts the foot (dorsiflexes) and turns its sole in
muscles.surface: a long belly just outside the shin edge; its tendon stands out in front of the ankle

muscles.name: Extensor digitorum longus and extensor hallucis longus
muscles.origin: upper fibula and lateral tibial condyle
muscles.insertion: toes, through tendons over the top of the foot
muscles.action: lift the toes and the foot
muscles.surface: between the tibialis and the peronei; tendons fan over the top of the foot

muscles.name: Peroneus longus and brevis
muscles.origin: outer fibula
muscles.insertion: longus: under the foot to the 1st metatarsal; brevis: base of the 5th metatarsal
muscles.action: turn the sole out (evert), point the foot
muscles.surface: a narrow band down the outer leg; the tendons curl behind the outer ankle bone

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.origin: two heads: back of the medial and lateral femoral condyles
muscles.insertion: calcaneus through the Achilles tendon
muscles.action: points the foot, bends the knee
muscles.surface: the calf: two heads, the inner one bigger and lower; they end in a W-shaped edge halfway down where the tendon begins

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.origin: back of the upper fibula and the soleal line of the tibia
muscles.insertion: calcaneus through the Achilles tendon
muscles.action: points the foot (standing, walking)
muscles.surface: widens the lower calf either side of the gastrocnemius; shows on both sides from the front

muscles.name: Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
muscles.origin: joined tendons of the gastrocnemius and soleus
muscles.insertion: back of the calcaneus
muscles.action: carries the calf pull to the heel
muscles.surface: a cord behind the ankle, narrowing then widening onto the heel, with hollows either side

muscles.name: Tibialis posterior and the long toe flexors
muscles.origin: back of the tibia and fibula and the interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: navicular and the bones of the sole; the toes
muscles.action: point and invert the foot, hold the arch
muscles.surface: deep; their tendons curl behind the inner ankle bone

fat.where: cheek, in front of the masseter
fat.change: hollows the cheek when lean; rounds the face when heavy
softens the jaw line from the side

fat.female: a teardrop resting on the pectoral, lower half fuller, about rib 2 to rib 6
fat.change: the female chest form; drawn as clothed or simplified volume in PG art, never detailed
rounds the lower belly forward; hides the lowest rectus

fat.where: over the iliac crest, at the side of the waist
fat.male: the "love handle": the first place a man gains
fat.change: rolls over the iliac crest and hides the oblique

fat.where: over the gluteus maximus and the hip
fat.female: thick: rounds the buttock and makes the gluteal fold
fat.change: makes the gluteal fold and the round of the buttock

fat.where: outer upper thigh below the trochanter
fat.female: thick ("saddle"): makes the trochanter the widest point

build_fat.rule: Fat fills hollows first (between muscles, over the trochanter, at the flank), then rounds the forms. A lean build shows tendons and the gaps between muscles; a heavy build shows the fat pads above, not bigger muscles.

measurements.unit: heads (crown to chin); cm at the reference stature: man 175 cm (head 23.3 cm), woman 162 cm (head 21.9 cm)

checklist.check: Stature in heads matches the figure (7.5 man, 7.4 woman; heroic 8 to 8.5)
checklist.how: crown to floor / crown to chin

checklist.check: The crotch sits at half the stature
Pit, nipples, navel, wrist, knee and ankle within tolerance of the canon (score_body.py)
Ribcage is an egg, narrow at the top, tilted back about 10 degrees; costal arch visible on a lean figure
Pelvis tilts forward; the ASIS and iliac crest are where the canon puts them; woman wider than her ribcage
S-curve from the side: neck forward, thoracic back, lumbar hollow; plumb line ear, shoulder, hip, ankle

Every surface=True bone landmark shows as a plane change or knob: clavicle, acromion, C7, scapula spine, elbow epicondyles, olecranon, wrist styloids, iliac crest, ASIS, trochanter dimple, kneecap, tibial tuberosity, shin, malleoli
Joints bend on the right axes with the ROM in the joints table; no joint bends past it
checklist.how: pose test: full range each joint

checklist.check: Raising the arm overhead also turns the scapula and lifts the clavicle (2 to 1)
Straight arm angles out at the elbow, palms forward
Sternocleidomastoid V into the pit; trapezius slope from neck to shoulder
Pectoral plate with its lower edge folding into the armpit; deltoid wedge into the arm
Rectus with three intersections above the navel only; external oblique flank over the iliac crest; serratus fingers on the ribs
Trapezius kite, latissimus V, erector columns with the furrow, shoulder blades as plates
Biceps in front, triceps horseshoe and tendon plate behind; brachialis shows either side of the biceps
Bellies in the upper half, tendons below; the outer mass (brachioradialis) starts above the elbow and is separate from the extensors
Outer thigh bulge higher than the inner teardrop; sartorius S divides quads from adductors; front of the thigh bows forward
Gluteus medius fullness under the iliac crest; buttock the furthest point back; trochanter hollow on a lean man
Kneecap with the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity; hamstring cords behind; the knee box sits between two cylinders
Calf: inner head lower than the outer, soleus wider below; shin straight; Achilles cord with hollows either side
Fat pads follow the sex and build (fat table): a woman's gluteal and lateral-thigh pads make the trochanters her widest point; a man's gather at the flank
A lean build shows the gaps between muscles and the tendons (wrist, ankle, back of the knee); a heavy build hides them under pads, not bigger muscles
No limb bulges on both edges at the same height (construction.json limb rules)
checklist.how: trace both edges of each limb

checklist.check: Planes read before detail: 6 to 8 per limb; folds only where bone is near the skin
PG: underwear or a smooth mannequin form, no genitals, nothing sexualised; breast is a simple clothed volume
